title: Adjective Agreement 3: Mixed Stems
description: A third class of adjectives looks like a mix of hard and soft endings: хороший, русский, маленький, большой. Today we drill their forms as a unit; Lesson 4 returns to the spelling rules that make them look mixed.
descriptionRussian: Третий класс прилагательных: основа кончается на шипящий или заднеязычный согласный. Слова: хороший, русский, маленький, большой. Сегодня — формы; правописание разбирается в уроке 4.
intro: This lesson deliberately asks you to memorize before it explains. That is not laziness. These four adjectives are common enough that you need them working this week, and the account of why their shapes look odd is a spelling rule in three parts that lands far better once the forms already sound right in your mouth. Take the paradigms as rhythms for now. Lesson 4 will show you they were never irregular at all.
rules: To spot a mixed-stem adjective, cover the ending and look at the last letter of the stem. If it is к, г, х (a velar) or ж, ш, ч, щ (a husher), the adjective is in today's class: хорош-ий, русск-ий, маленьк-ий, больш-ой. This is the only reliable test, because the ending alone will fool you: синий ends in -ий too, but син- ends in н, so синий is a soft stem from Lesson 2.
The four forms of хороший are хороший (m sg), хорошая (f sg), хорошее (n sg), хорошие (pl). Memorize the paradigm as a single rhythmic unit.
Маленький and русский pattern alike: -ий for masculine, -ая for feminine, -ое for neuter, -ие for plural. Even though they look mixed, the agreement choice is still gender plus number.
Большой stresses the masculine ending: большой (m sg, stressed -ой), большая (f sg), большое (n sg), большие (pl). The other forms keep regular stresses on the ending.

Two endings never vary in this class, whatever else does. The feminine is always -ая (хорошая, русская, маленькая, большая) and the plural is always -ие, never -ые (хорошие, русские, маленькие, большие). Lean on those two while the masculine and neuter forms settle.
examples: Это хороший день. (This is a good day.) День is masculine singular: the masculine form is хороший.
Это русская книга. (This is a Russian book.) Книга is feminine singular: the feminine form is русская.
Это маленькое окно. (This is a small window.) Окно is neuter singular: the neuter form is маленькое.
В лесу большие деревья. (There are big trees in the forest.) Деревья is plural: the plural form is большие.
У Маши хорошее задание. (Masha has a good assignment.) Задание is neuter singular: the neuter form is хорошее. Compare маленькое: same -ое neuter ending, even though хорошее has the husher -ш- stem.
В Москве большой парк. (There is a big park in Moscow.) Парк is masculine singular: большой is the stressed-ending masculine form.

items.hint: Warm-up from Lesson 2. Песня is feminine singular: which soft-stem ending fits?
items.explanation: Recall from Lesson 2: soft-stem feminine singular takes -яя. Песня ends in -я (feminine), so последняя. Today's class adds a third pattern that includes some adjectives ending in -ий like синий but with different feminine and neuter forms.

items.hint: День is masculine singular. The mixed-stem masculine form of хороший ends in -ий, like a soft adjective.
items.explanation: День is masculine singular. The masculine form of хороший is хороший, written with soft -ий even though the rest of the paradigm has hard endings. Lesson 4 explains why; today, learn the surface form.

items.hint: Книга is feminine singular. The feminine form of русский looks fully hard.
items.explanation: Книга is feminine singular. The feminine form is русская, with regular hard -ая. The spelling wrinkle in this adjective class does not affect the -ая ending, only the masculine and plural forms (Lesson 4 returns to this).

items.hint: Окно is neuter singular. The neuter form of маленький keeps the regular -ое ending.
items.explanation: Окно is neuter singular. The neuter form is маленькое, with regular -ое. The same -ое ending works on русское and большое: the spelling wrinkle does not show up in the neuter form here because the ending is unstressed and follows the regular pattern.

items.promptEnglish: There are big trees in the forest.
items.hint: Деревья is plural. The plural form is the same across all genders.
items.explanation: Деревья is plural. The plural form is большие. Like хорошие and маленькие, the plural form ends in -ие (not -ые). Lesson 4 unpacks the spelling rule; for now, lock in 'большие' as the only plural form for big.

items.hint: Задание is neuter singular. The neuter form of хороший is unstressed and uses the soft-vowel -ее ending.
items.explanation: Задание is neuter singular. The neuter form is хорошее, written with -ее (not -ое). The stem ends in -ш-, and after ш with an unstressed ending, Russian writes -е not -о. Lesson 4 returns to this rule; today, lock хорошее as the neuter form.

blanks: Дома живёт _____ кошка. (A small cat lives at home.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Кошка is feminine singular. The feminine form of маленький is маленькая, with regular hard -ая. The same -ая ending works on every mixed-stem adjective in the feminine form: хорошая, русская, большая.

errorCorrection.sentence: Это хороший школа в нашем районе.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: This is a good school in our neighborhood.
errorCorrection.explanation: Школа is feminine, so the adjective takes the feminine -ая ending: хорошая. Mixed-stem adjectives use the same gender endings as hard stems in the feminine; the spelling rule only changes -ы to -и. Хороший is the masculine form.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: This is a Russian magazine about culture.
errorCorrection.explanation: Журнал is masculine, so the adjective takes the masculine form: русский (the spelling rule turns the usual -ый into -ий after к). Русская is the feminine form and does not match the masculine noun журнал.

errorCorrection.sentence: В Москве большая парк, где гуляют дети с родителями.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: There's a big park in Moscow where children walk with their parents.
errorCorrection.explanation: Парк is masculine, so the adjective takes the masculine ending. Большой belongs to a small subgroup whose masculine ending is the STRESSED -о́й (rather than unstressed -ый): большой, молодой, другой, золотой. So 'a big park' is большой парк.

minimalPairs.explanation: Дом is masculine singular: the masculine form is маленький. Маленькое would require a neuter noun like окно or озеро.
Парки is plural: the plural form is большие. Большой is the masculine singular and would require one specific park (большой парк).

categorySorting.instruction: Sort these adjectives by stem class.

reviewVocab.definition: mixed stem (the adjective class whose stem ends in a velar к/г/х or a husher ж/ш/ч/щ; includes хороший, русский, маленький, большой)
reviewVocab.example: Прилагательное 'хороший' имеет смешанную основу: основа кончается на шипящий -ш-.

reviewVocab.definition: husher (one of the consonants ж, ш, ч, щ; in adjective endings, hushers trigger the -и / -е spelling rules covered in Lesson 4)
reviewVocab.example: Шипящий звук в основе слова 'хороший' влияет на формы 'хорошие' и 'хорошее'.

reviewVocab.definition: velar, back-lingual (one of the consonants к, г, х; also triggers the -и spelling rule in adjective endings)
reviewVocab.example: В прилагательном 'маленький' заднеязычный согласный -к- даёт окончание -ие во множественном числе.

patternRecognition.question: Cover the ending. What does the stem of русский end in?
options: Mixed stem: velar к, г, х
Mixed stem: husher ж, ш, ч, щ
patternRecognition.answer: Mixed stem: velar к, г, х
patternRecognition.explanation: Русск- ends in к, a velar, so русский is in today's class. Note that the -ий ending told you nothing on its own: синий ends in -ий as well and is a soft stem.

patternRecognition.question: Same test on синий. What does its stem end in?
options: Mixed stem: velar к, г, х
Mixed stem: husher ж, ш, ч, щ
patternRecognition.explanation: Син- ends in н. That is neither a velar nor a husher, so синий is not a mixed stem; it is the soft-stem type from Lesson 2 (синий, синяя, синее, синие). Русский and синий look alike in the masculine and part company everywhere else.

patternRecognition.question: Свежий (fresh) is a new word. Run the test: which class is it in?
options: Mixed stem: velar к, г, х
Mixed stem: husher ж, ш, ч, щ
patternRecognition.answer: Mixed stem: husher ж, ш, ч, щ
patternRecognition.explanation: Свеж- ends in ж, a husher, so свежий joins today's class even though you have not drilled its forms. That is the point of the test: it works on adjectives you have never seen.

patternRecognition.question: And красный?
options: Mixed stem: velar к, г, х
Mixed stem: husher ж, ш, ч, щ
patternRecognition.explanation: Красн- ends in н, so красный is an ordinary hard stem: красный, красная, красное, красные, with the plural -ые. Compare русские and хорошие, where the plural is -ие instead. That difference is the practical payoff of spotting the class.
